config_path.description: The path where the generated wrapper script will be saved.

rules_file.description: Path to the Yara rules file (.yar or compiled .yarx).

target.description: The file, directory, or PID to scan.

target_type.description: The type of target being scanned. Used to clarify intent, though Yara accepts files, dirs, and PIDs.

compiled_rules.description: Set to true if RULES_FILE contains rules already compiled with yarac (-C).

fast_scan.description: Speeds up scanning by searching only for the first occurrence of each pattern (-f).

recursive.description: Scan files in directories recursively and follow symlinks (-r).

strict_escape.description: Print warnings if rules contain ambiguous escape statements (--strict-escape).

max_rules.description: Abort scanning after this number of rules matched (-l). 0 means no limit.

threads.description: Use this number of threads to scan a directory (-p).

timeout.description: Abort scanning after this many seconds (-a). 0 means no timeout.

skip_larger.description: Skip files larger than this size in bytes when scanning a directory (-z). 0 means no limit.

external_variables.description: List of external variables to define with -d. Each item is a flat map with 'identifier' and 'value'. See items schema below.

tags.description: List of tags to filter rules. Only rules with these tags are printed (-t).

identifiers.description: List of rule identifiers to filter rules. Only rules with these names are printed (-i).

module_data_list.description: List of module data mappings to pass to modules with -x. Each item is a flat map with 'module' and 'file'. See items schema below.

print_meta.description: Print metadata associated to the rule (-m).

print_strings.description: Print strings found in the file (-s).

print_string_length.description: Print length of strings found in the file (-L).

print_xor_key.description: Print xor key of matched strings (-X).

print_tags.description: Print the tags associated to the rule (-g).

scan_list.description: If true, the TARGET is a file containing a list of files to scan, one per line (--scan-list).
